subject: red sea urchin
title: This Sea Urchin Can Live 200 Years and Never Seems to Get Old

scenes.text: Scientists thought this sea urchin lived ten years. Some were alive before the first car.
Red sea urchins off the Pacific coast of North America can live past one hundred years.
The biggest ones, off British Columbia, are estimated at over two hundred.
Researchers proved it with carbon left by nuclear bomb tests, and a second method agreed.
And the old ones don't slow down. A hundred-year-old breeds as well as a ten-year-old, and still regrows lost spines.
So what kills them? Otters, disease and fishing. Not old age.

description:
Red sea urchins, once assumed to live 7 to 15 years, can live more than 100, and the largest off British Columbia are estimated at over 200 (Oregon State University and Lawrence Livermore, 2003).
Old urchins keep reproducing, and a 2016 Aging Cell study found their ability to regrow spines does not decline with age.
What animal do you think lives longest?
first_comment: The researcher said a 100-year-old urchin is just as likely to live another year as a 10-year-old. Which animal would you want to swap lifespans with?
